_: Who can appear in the communication window. A speaker named here by the @Name in a .oddlg script gets these numbers; one that is not named still appears, as a silhouette derived from its own name, so a script can introduce a character before anybody has drawn one.
_image: A greyscale PNG in data/comms/. It carries NO colour: the filter takes the player's accent. tools/comms_signal.py makes one from a drawing; tools/comms_derive.py makes the other two out of the same drawing.
_voice: The blip this character makes while typing. data/audio/sfx/voice/voice_<name>_1..6.wav; the engine strips the number and picks between takes, so a line never machine-guns one sample. tools/make_voices.py generates them.
_eyes: eye_y, eye_gap, eye_w and eye_h are fractions of the IMAGE. They place the live eyes over the art, which is the only part of a speaker that moves. Set "eyes": false for a speaker whose face is not shown. Set "lid_bottom": true for an eye that closes from below, which reads as a smile rather than as fatigue.

Signals Officer._: Mia, from her own .kra. Her eyes and mouth are NOT in the art -- their Krita layers are switched off by tools/kra_export.py -- because they are the parts that move. The window draws them, in her shape.

Cryptographer._: The unknown speaker: a figure with the light off it and a question mark where a face would be. No eyes -- that is the whole idea of them.

Pr1nted._: The developer, talking to the player from outside the game. Same drawing as the Advisor -- it is the same person; the Advisor is who he plays in a scripted briefing and Pr1nted is who he is when he rings up about the tutorial.

_mouth: A speaker with "mouth": true has one drawn by the window instead of baked into the art: one curve whose bow is the mood and whose opening is the glyph being typed. Paint the mouth out of the art (comms_signal.py --mouth) and give the coordinates it prints.
_display: What the plate says. `display` is the name and `role` what they are. The KEY stays the formal name because a .oddlg keys on it and an id must not move; the plate is what the player reads. The portrait shows the name alone -- the role belongs on the textbox, beside the words.
